 Try reading from the online pre-calc source

```{r}
library(data.table)

ld_file <- "/path/to/project/Other data/Correlation matrix for CBX8/gtex_v8_expression_mashr_snp_covariance.txt"

## ---------- 1. Verify awk availability ----------
have_awk <- nzchar(Sys.which("awk"))

## ---------- 2. Build the reader ----------
if (have_awk) {
  ## Windows needs the file path in *double* quotes; awk script in *single* quotes
  awk_cmd <- sprintf(
    "awk \"($2 ~ /^chr17_/ || $3 ~ /^chr17_/ )\" \"%s\"",
    ld_file
  )
  
  message("Reading via awk stream-filter …")
  ld17 <- fread(
    cmd         = awk_cmd,
    sep         = " ",                     # space-delimited
    header      = FALSE,
    col.names   = c("GENE", "RSID1", "RSID2", "VALUE"),
    colClasses  = c("character", "character", "character", "numeric"),
    showProgress = FALSE
  )
  
} else {
  message("awk not found – falling back to in-R filtering (needs a bit more RAM).")
  
  ## read only the columns we need, then filter
  ld <- fread(
    ld_file,
    sep        = " ",
    select     = 2:4,                      # drop the GENE column up-front
    col.names  = c("RSID1", "RSID2", "VALUE"),
    colClasses = c("character", "character", "numeric"),
    nThread    = 8                         # adjust to your CPU
  )
  ld17 <- ld[grepl("^chr17_", RSID1) | grepl("^chr17_", RSID2)]
}

## ---------- 3. Subset to your focal variants ----------
z_scores <- fread("/path/to/project/susine/data/CBX8 Study/GTEx v10 CBX8 Lung SNP z_scores.csv")
targets_chr17 <- z_scores$variant_id       # already chr17-only in your file

ld_sub <- ld17[
  RSID1 %in% targets_chr17 & RSID2 %in% targets_chr17
]


```

```{r}
# --- 1)  Your two data frames -----------------------------------------------
# df_pairs    : the “long” table with RSID1, RSID2, VALUE   (first screenshot)
# variants_df : the one-column table with variant_id        (second screenshot)

# Example names (rename if yours differ):
# df_pairs    <- your_first_dataframe
# variants_df <- your_second_dataframe

# --- 2)  Fix the variant order you want --------------------------------------
var_order <- z_scores$variant_id        # keep the original order
n         <- length(var_order)

# --- 3)  If the pair table has multiple rows per pair (e.g. different genes),
#         pick ONE value per pair – here I take the mean ----------------------
library(dplyr)

ld_pairs <- ld_sub                                      %>% 
  filter(RSID1 %in% var_order & RSID2 %in% var_order)      %>%  # keep only needed SNPs
  group_by(RSID1, RSID2)                                   %>% 
  summarise(VALUE = mean(VALUE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

# --- 4)  Build an empty square matrix and fill it ----------------------------
ld_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n,
                 dimnames = list(var_order, var_order))
diag(ld_mat) <- 1                                            # self-LD = 1

# fill the upper & lower triangles
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ld_pairs))) {
  snp1 <- ld_pairs$RSID1[i]
  snp2 <- ld_pairs$RSID2[i]
  val  <- ld_pairs$VALUE[i]
  
  ld_mat[snp1, snp2] <- val
  ld_mat[snp2, snp1] <- val      # symmetry
}

# --- 5)  (Optional) replace any still-missing cells --------------------------
# For example, NA → 0 (or keep NA if you prefer):
ld_mat[is.na(ld_mat)] <- 0

save(ld_mat, file="CBX8_lung_R.Rdata")
getwd()

```
